## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pasannacitta Sutta* ("A Pure Mind", Iti 21) is a short discourse in the *Ekakanipāta* of the *Itivuttaka* (PTS It 13). The sutta delivers the concise teaching that clear-mindedness and mental purity (*pasannacitta*) lead directly to rebirth in a heavenly realm. It forms a complementary doctrinal pair with the preceding *Paduṭṭhacitta Sutta* (Iti 20), which describes the opposite fate of a corrupted mind; DharmaNexus records 1,529 matching characters between the two texts across segments §0.1–6.2 [DharmaNexus].

 The text is also cited in the exegetical treatise *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37, *Sāsanapaṭṭhāna*), an inclusion confirmed both by curated references and by DharmaNexus text-reuse matches showing extensive alignment between Iti 21 (§2.1–6.1) and Ne 37 (§109.1–113.1) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus indicates shared formulas and textual reuse across numerous Pāli works, notably the *Ekakanipāta* (AN 1), *Mahāsīhanāda Sutta* (MN 12), *Chakkanipāta* (AN 6), *Posālamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 18), and *Nettivibhāvinī* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matches, DharmaNexus automatically aligns the sutta with the Sanskrit *Mahākarmavibhaṅga* [DharmaNexus]. The reference literature passages located for this entry merely match the common lexical compound *pasannacitta* across other contexts rather than commenting on this discourse.
